diagnosis.summary: Request rates across all four services have risen sharply above baseline in the current one-minute window, with product-service up 6.4x, cart-service up 11.3x, order-service up 10.3x, and payment-service up 16.3x. DynamoDB capacity consumption has risen on all three tables in proportion with the higher request rates. Product-service error_rate_5xx remains at 0 and order-service p50 latency, while elevated, is still in the low milliseconds.
diagnosis.root_cause: A broad, simultaneous traffic spike across all four services is the most likely root cause, with no single service isolated.
evidence: Request rates rose across all four services: product-service from 14.98 to 96.23 rps (6.4x), cart-service from 2.05 to 23.2 rps (11.3x), order-service from 2.97 to 30.45 rps (10.3x), and payment-service from 0.94 to 15.35 rps (16.3x).
Product-service DynamoDB read capacity rose from 449 to 2,887 RCU/min, a 6.4x increase.
Order-service DynamoDB read capacity rose from 60.8 to 453 RCU/min and write capacity rose from 56.6 to 921 WCU/min (16.3x).
Cart-service DynamoDB write capacity rose from 122.8 to 1,392 WCU/min, an 11.3x increase.
Order-service p50 latency rose from 3.6 ms to 12.4 ms, a 3.5x increase above baseline.
Product-service error_rate_5xx is 0, unchanged from its baseline of 0.
recommended_actions: Determine whether the traffic spike is expected (a promotion, a launch, or a client stuck retrying) before making any configuration changes.
Monitor lambda_throttle_count on all four services to detect whether the shared Lambda concurrency limit is being reached; throttled invocations would not appear in the recorded request rates.

Watch product-service read_throttle_events and db_consumed_read_capacity closely; if reads continue rising toward table capacity limits, raise the Products table provisioned read capacity or switch it to on-demand.
If latency and error rates hold near baseline as they currently do, continue monitoring without immediate changes.
To protect the stack while investigating the traffic source, consider setting rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage.
